technical_data.additional_notes: The attacker used the legitimate company domain and a compromised internal mail server (192.0.2.45) to send the email, making it highly convincing. The personalized bank details in the email body were crafted from leaked vendor payment information obtained from previous data breaches.

indicators: Email from ceo@company-example.com sent from atypical outbound IP 192.0.2.45 not normally used for CEO emails
Urgent payment request with new bank details differing from previously used vendor accounts
URL contains redirect parameter pointing to external banking site used for credential harvesting
Authentication-Results showing DKIM and SPF pass but unusual sending pattern noted in SIEM
Email subject includes urgent financial terms combined with personalized user name
examples.detection_method: Monitor outbound email traffic for deviations in sending IPs and volume from executive accounts; Implement advanced phishing detection tools analyzing email content for payment request context; Correlate new bank account details in emails with vendor payment history; Employ user training simulations emphasizing CEO impersonation and urgent invoice requests; Use URL rewriting and scanning to detect redirect-based phishing links.
